title: Vertiv Announces Dynamic Online Mode and New, Smaller Modules of High Power Density UPS Family
summary: Vertiv introduced Dynamic Online mode to the Liebert EXL S1 to meet the needs of cloud, colocation and enterprise data centers that cannot sacrifice any level of availability for incremental gains in efficiency. With efficiency up to 99 percent, the Liebert EXL S1 operating in Dynamic Online mode offers substantial energy savings over legacy UPS systems that average 94 percent efficiency, and even improves on modern UPS systems that approach 97 percent.
body_text: Columbus, Ohio [March 21, 2019] – Vertiv today announced a new feature for the Liebert® EXL S1 line of uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems, adding Dynamic Online mode , which allows operating efficiency of up to 99 percent without compromising availability. In addition, Vertiv introduced 500 and 600 kVA 480V module ratings for the Liebert EXL S1. The UPS family is available now in North America in eight capacity ratings from 500 kVA to 1200 kVA, 480V. The UPS is also available in Europe and Asia Pacific in 100 to 1200 kVA capacities and a variety of input and output voltages. Dynamic Online mode is available for Liebert EXL S1 globally. Vertiv introduced Dynamic Online mode to the Liebert EXL S1 to meet the needs of cloud, colocation and enterprise data centers that cannot sacrifice any level of availability for incremental gains in efficiency. With efficiency up to 99 percent, the Liebert EXL S1 operating in Dynamic Online mode offers substantial energy savings over legacy UPS systems that average 94 percent efficiency, and even improves on modern UPS systems that approach 97 percent. Over five years, a 1000 kVA Liebert EXL S1 can save more than $230,000 over a same-capacity 94 percent efficient UPS system and more than $140,000 over a same-capacity 97 percent efficient UPS system. “As energy consumption has become increasingly important across the data center, Vertiv has been a leader in the development of highly efficient infrastructure solutions that deliver best-in-class network availability,” said Franco Costa, vice president of global AC power for Vertiv. “With the addition of Dynamic Online Mode and extension of our Liebert EXL S1 UPS line, we further expand our portfolio to deliver a wider range of reliable, efficient solutions to customers who strive to optimize their infrastructure and operations while maintaining the highest level of availability for their service level agreements.” While in Dynamic Online mode, the Liebert EXL S1 inverter can instantaneously assume the load and maintain the output voltage well within the IEC 62040-3 Class 1 specification. That means systems equipped with Dynamic Online mode can safely transition from high-efficiency (Voltage Independent) mode to inverter mode with a near-zero-millisecond transfer, thus providing absolute load power protection under virtually any input power outage condition. The new models of Liebert EXL S1 are up to 40 percent smaller than competitive systems and designed to meet the reliability and flexibility demands of the modern data center. Redundant DC variable speed fans enable the UPS to support 100 percent load even with multiple fan failures. Various input/output options add flexibility and reduce capital and installation costs. As with previously released Liebert EXL S1 modules, customers can parallel up to eight units and leverage Intelligent Parallel mode to automatically optimize efficiency at reduced load levels. The system’s touchscreen interface offers a status-at-a-glance LED light bar, customizable views and multiple security options, while intelligent controls ensure seamless integration with multiple Vertiv and third-party building management and data center infrastructure management systems. All sizes of the Liebert EXL S1 UPS are available with lithium-ion batteries , flywheels, Alber® battery monitoring , and LIFE™ Services . For more information on the Liebert EXL S1 and other UPS solutions from Vertiv, visit Vertiv.com . For more information about high-efficiency modes of operation, download the latest Vertiv white paper . About Vertiv Vertiv brings together hardware, software, analytics and ongoing services to ensure its customers’ vital applications run continuously, perform optimally and grow with their business needs. Vertiv solves the most important challenges facing today’s data centers, communication networks and commercial and industrial facilities with a portfolio of power, cooling and IT infrastructure solutions and services that extends from the cloud to the edge of the network. Headquartered in Columbus, Ohio, USA, Vertiv employs around 20,000 people and does business in more than 130 countries. For more information, and for the latest news and content from Vertiv, visit Vertiv.com . CONTACT Vince McMorrow T +614 383 1622 E Vince.McMorrow@Fahlgren.com

title: More than a sale: Planning for life after the business exit
summary: After spending decades building a company, many business owners imagine the sale itself as the finish line. Discover how to prepare for what comes next.
body_text: After spending decades building a company, many business owners imagine the sale itself as the finish line. The transaction closes, the wire payment arrives and years of hard work finally culminate in financial success. But for many business owners, the closing table is not simply the ending, but rather the beginning of a completely different challenge. Entrepreneurs spend years learning how to build wealth, but far fewer spend time preparing for what comes next. The strongest companies are often positioned to sell well before the owner intends to exit. True readiness to sell goes beyond financial performance and should begin one to five years before going to market. Creating a business exit vision Before owners decide whether they want to sell, they first need to answer a personal question: What do they want life to look like after the exit? Are they stepping away completely? Starting another company? Do they hope the sale will provide for future generations or support meaningful philanthropy? The emotional side of an exit is often underestimated. For many founders, the business was never simply an income source. It was purpose, structure, relationships and often, identity. Selling can create unexpected questions: Who am I now? What do I do next? How involved should I remain? Without that clarity, it becomes difficult to know how much is enough, how the business should be structured and what risks should be addressed before the sale. Liquidity adds complexity One sentence business owners often share six months after a sale is, “My life is busier now than when I was running my business.” That’s because liquidity can create complexity overnight. A concentrated business asset may suddenly become substantial cash, and with that comes immediate decisions involving taxes, investment strategy, estate planning, philanthropy, family governance and risk management. For many owners, managing wealth becomes an entirely new job—but preparing for it ahead of time can help mitigate the risk of costly mistakes and relieve the pressure that often comes with major financial decisions. Some owners wait too long to begin planning and miss opportunities to save millions in taxes simply because the business or estate structure wasn’t optimized well in advance of the sale. Others discover they have outdated insurance coverage or weak asset protection at the exact moment their financial visibility increases. Even private transactions can create exposure, lawsuits or unwanted attention if risk management has not been reviewed carefully. Investment strategy is another common issue. Many owners continue managing their wealth the same way they managed their business, holding concentrated risk. Others become overly conservative because they fear losing what they worked so hard to build. Investment management matters, but coordination of attorneys, CPAs, insurance specialists and bankers often matters more. Post business sale, families increasingly want a wealth advisor that can serve as a “financial quarterback” to help organize the entire picture. The process usually begins with data gathering to organize everything in one place: account statements, insurance policies, trusts, estate documents, tax returns and existing advisory relationships. From there, the focus becomes defining goals and identifying where advice overlaps, conflicts or leaves gaps. The quarterback will coordinate with the team and develop trust, so owners don’t feel they are alone after the sale. In some cases, people may realize they’ve outgrown their current network. As wealth grows, so does the complexity surrounding it, and not every advisory team is built to navigate an eight- or nine-figure liquidity event. How to secure a smooth transition The best transitions often involve organizing wealth with intent. One framework is a bucket approach: a liquidity bucket for near-term cash needs and lifestyle, a long-term investment bucket for growth and a legacy bucket for future generations, philanthropy or charitable goals. When each bucket has a purpose, decision-making becomes clearer. Most importantly, owners stop managing everything alone. The right banking and wealth management team communicates regularly, understands the family’s objectives and ensures everyone is aligned. That coordination reduces decision fatigue, prevents expensive mistakes and allows owners to enjoy the wealth they created. Selling a company can be one of life’s greatest achievements, but creating wealth and managing wealth require entirely different skillsets. If you’re a business owner looking to sell in the future, find your quarterback now so you can approach the exit with clarity, confidence, and purpose. title: 2026 Wedding Trends: What Couples Are Actually Doing This Year
summary: The defining theme of 2026 weddings is intentionality. Couples are designing celebrations that reflect who they are, prioritizing guest experience over
body_text: Last Updated on July 23, 2026 by Joy Editors The defining theme of 2026 weddings is intentionality . Couples are designing celebrations that reflect who they are, prioritizing guest experience over spectacle, scaling back guest counts to reinvest in quality, and replacing rigid traditions with personalized moments. Key trends: the wedding website as a central planning hub, experiential weddings, experience-based registries, destination and multi-day celebrations, opalescent color palettes, deconstructed timelines, and intimate guest counts. Every year brings a new wave of wedding trends, but 2026 feels different. The shift is less about aesthetics and more about attitude. Couples getting married this year are asking a different set of questions: not “what does a wedding look like?” but “what do we want our guests to feel?” Here are the trends shaping 2026 weddings, based on input from planners, vendor data, and patterns across the more than 2 million couples who have used Joy to plan their weddings. 1. The Wedding Website as the Central Planning Hub A growing trend in 2026 is treating the wedding website as the single destination for everything guests need to know. Rather than sending separate messages for RSVPs, hotel details, registry links, and day-of logistics, couples are consolidating it all into one place. This shift reflects how guests actually behave. When someone receives a save-the-date or invitation, the first thing they do is check the wedding website. If they can find the RSVP , hotel block details , the schedule, and the registry in one place, fewer follow-up questions end up in the couple’s inbox. Couples are building out their wedding websites with guest list management , RSVP tracking, accommodation details with booking deadlines, transportation logistics , and registry links. The website has evolved from a formality into the operational backbone of the wedding. 2. Experiential Weddings Designed Around the Guest The biggest aesthetic shift in 2026 is that couples are planning weddings from the guest’s point of view. Instead of focusing on how the day looks, they are asking: “What will my guests feel at each moment?” This shows up in concrete ways: thoughtful welcome experiences (interactive drink stations, personalized signage), cocktail hours that feel like a destination, lounge-style layouts that encourage movement and conversation, and transitions between parts of the day that feel intentional rather than rushed. Traditional wedding favors are being replaced by moments. Couples are opting for handwritten notes at place settings, shared experiences, or locally sourced keepsakes tied to their story. If guests would not take it home or remember it, the trend is to skip it entirely. 3. Experience-Based Registries Continue Growing The traditional registry model (dishes, towels, appliances) is not disappearing, but it is being supplemented and in many cases replaced by experience-based options. More couples in 2026 are creating honeymoon funds and cash funds that let guests contribute to experiences rather than physical gifts. Honeymoon funds are especially popular among couples who already live together and do not need household items. Instead of a third set of wine glasses, guests can contribute toward a specific honeymoon experience: a cooking class in Tuscany, a snorkeling excursion in the Maldives , or simply a travel fund the couple can apply wherever they choose. Cash funds serve a broader purpose. Couples are using them for down payments, student loan payoffs, home renovations, or “date night” funds. The appeal is flexibility: guests give something meaningful, and the couple puts it toward what matters most to them right now. This trend also pairs with the shift toward smaller, more intentional celebrations. When couples trim the guest list and invest more in the experience, guests often respond with more generous, purposeful gifts. 4. Intimate Guest Counts with Elevated Execution Smaller weddings are back, but with a different motivation than pandemic-era micro weddings. In 2026, couples are choosing smaller guest counts deliberately, then reinvesting the budget into the people who are there. Smaller guest counts allow for deeper personalization, better food, more meaningful interactions, and a celebration that feels connected rather than crowded. The focus has shifted from how many people attend to how those guests feel. This does not mean micro weddings only. Many couples are trimming from 200 guests to 80-100, which still feels like a full celebration but allows for a higher per-guest experience budget. 5. Destination and Multi-Day Celebrations Destination weddings and multi-day celebrations are gaining momentum in 2026, driven by couples who want the wedding to feel like a shared experience rather than a single event. The focus has shifted from just the ceremony and reception to the entire guest journey: welcome dinners, morning-after brunches, group activities, and coordinated travel. What makes this trend different from previous years is the emphasis on guest experience logistics. Couples are thinking through every touchpoint: How will guests get from the airport to the hotel? Is there a welcome bag waiting? Is the schedule clear enough that guests can plan their own downtime? This requires more planning infrastructure. Couples hosting multi-day celebrations are leaning heavily on their wedding websites to communicate schedules, hotel block information with booking deadlines, shuttle details , and local recommendations. For destination weddings in particular, centralizing this information prevents the barrage of “where should I stay?” and “how do I get there?” texts that would otherwise overwhelm the couple. The multi-day format also changes how couples think about food, entertainment, and pacing. Rather than front-loading everything into four hours, the celebration can breathe across multiple events, giving guests time to connect and the couple time to actually enjoy each moment. 6. Opalescent and Nature-Inspired Color Palettes The dominant color story of 2026 weddings has two threads running in parallel: opalescent and iridescent palettes on one end, and warm nature-inspired neutrals on the other. Opalescent palettes draw from pearl, champagne, soft lavender, and iridescent whites. They photograph beautifully in natural light and create a dreamlike, cinematic quality. On the warmer side, couples are choosing soft neutrals with intentional accents: champagne, terracotta, deep navy, muted sage, and warm whites. These palettes feel timeless, work in both indoor and outdoor settings, and avoid the “trendy” problem of looking dated in photos five years from now. Bold jewel tones (deep burgundy, forest green, cobalt) are also trending for couples who want more visual impact, particularly for fall and winter weddings. Palette Style Colors Best For Opalescent Pearl, champagne, soft lavender, iridescent white Spring and summer, garden venues, natural light Warm neutrals Champagne, terracotta, warm white, muted sage Year-round, indoor and outdoor, timeless look Bold jewel tones Deep burgundy, forest green, cobalt, deep navy Fall and winter, evening receptions, dramatic settings Coastal elegance Soft blue, sandy beige, warm white, natural textures Waterfront venues, coastal locations 7. Statement Lighting as a Design Element Lighting has moved from a functional afterthought to a primary design decision. In 2026, couples are treating lighting the way they treat florals: as a major visual element that sets the mood for the entire event. Floating chandeliers, hanging lantern clusters, oversized pendants, warm uplighting, and candle-heavy tablescapes are all trending. The goal is an immersive atmosphere that photographs well and feels different from a standard hotel ballroom. For couples working with a tight budget, lighting is one of the highest-impact investments available. A simple venue with exceptional lighting often looks more impressive than an expensive venue with flat overhead lighting. 8. Deconstructed Wedding Timelines The traditional wedding timeline (ceremony, cocktail hour, seated dinner, dancing) is being rethought. In 2026, couples are designing days that feel fluid rather than formulaic. Some couples are replacing seated dinners with cocktail-style receptions featuring roaming food presentations, live stations, and lounge vignettes. Others are extending cocktail hours into the main event, with the reception flowing continuously rather than breaking into distinct phases. Gen Z couples in particular are prioritizing vibe, music, and movement from the moment guests arrive, rather than following a traditional cadence. The focus is on keeping energy high throughout the day rather than building to a single peak moment. Planning note: A deconstructed timeline requires more coordination with your venue and caterer. Make sure your venue supports flexible layouts and that your catering team is comfortable with roaming service before committing to this format. 9. Content Creators Alongside (or Instead of) Videographers Traditional wedding videography is being supplemented or replaced by content creators who deliver short-form, behind-the-scenes footage optimized for social media. The style is more documentary and candid than a polished highlight reel. Couples who grew up with Instagram and TikTok want wedding content that feels authentic and shareable, not cinematic in the traditional sense. Content creators capture the moments between moments: the getting-ready chaos, the quiet exchange before the ceremony, the dance floor at 11pm. Many couples are hiring both: a traditional videographer for the formal highlight film and a content creator for day-of social content. 10. Personalized Ceremonies That Reflect the Couple Generic ceremonies are out. In 2026, couples are writing their own vows, choosing non-traditional officiants (friends, family members, or celebrants rather than clergy), and building ceremonies around their specific story rather than a standard template. Ceremony personalization extends to music (live string quartets are trending, partly due to the Bridgerton effect), readings from meaningful texts, and interactive elements like unity ceremonies that reflect the couple’s actual relationship rather than a tradition they inherited. 11. Longer Engagements and More Intentional Planning Engagement lengths are stretching to 18-24 months in 2026, driven by financial goals, career milestones, and a desire to plan more intentionally. Couples are not rushing to a date; they are using the engagement period to make thoughtful choices rather than quick decisions. This shift is changing how vendors work. Venues and photographers are booking further out, and couples are taking more time to research, compare, and personalize every element of the day. Longer engagements also mean more time to save, which is contributing to the elevated execution trend. Couples who plan for 20 months have more budget flexibility than those who plan for 10. 12. Throwback and Vintage Entertainment Nostalgia is a strong thread running through 2026 wedding entertainment. Couples are incorporating vintage and throwback elements: custom coin-operated sticker machines as favors, claw machines with prizes, arcade games, and entertainment that nods to their childhood. This trend pairs with the broader personalization shift. A couple who bonded over ’90s video games might set up a retro gaming station at the cocktail hour. A couple who met at a speakeasy might design their reception around that aesthetic. The goal is entertainment that tells a story about the couple, not entertainment that could belong to any wedding. What Is Going Out of Style in 2026 Trending out: Generic wedding favors guests do not want (candles, koozies, Jordan almonds) Overly themed weddings where the theme overwhelms the couple’s personality Rigid traditional timelines that feel formulaic One-size-fits-all ceremonies with no personal elements Maximalist floral arrangements that dominate the budget without adding to the experience Binary language and traditional frameworks that do not reflect the couple How to Use These Trends Without Losing Your Vision Trends are useful as a starting point, not a checklist. The couples who have the best weddings in 2026 are not the ones who incorporate every trend; they are the ones who know which trends resonate with them and ignore the rest. A few questions worth asking as you plan: Which of these trends feels like us, and which feels like something we are doing because we saw it on Instagram? If we removed this element, would our guests notice or care? Does this decision serve our guests, or does it serve a photo? A wedding website is the easiest way to organize every detail of your 2026 wedding in one place: RSVP management, guest list , registry and cash funds , and hotel blocks . Start planning for free. Frequently Asked Questions What are the biggest wedding trends in 2026? The biggest 2026 wedding trends are the wedding website as a central planning hub, experiential celebrations designed around the guest experience, experience-based registries including honeymoon and cash funds, destination and multi-day celebrations, smaller and more intimate guest counts, opalescent and nature-inspired color palettes, deconstructed timelines, statement lighting, and content creators supplementing traditional videographers. What wedding trends are going out of style in 2026? Wedding trends going out of style in 2026 include overly themed weddings, generic wedding favors guests do not want, rigid traditional timelines, and one-size-fits-all ceremonies that do not reflect the couple’s personality. What colors are trending for weddings in 2026? The top 2026 wedding color trends are opalescent and iridescent palettes, soft neutrals with warm accents (champagne, terracotta, deep navy), nature-inspired greens and muted blues, and bold jewel tones for couples who want more visual impact. Are small weddings still trending in 2026? Yes. Intimate weddings with smaller guest counts are a strong trend in 2026. Couples are scaling back guest lists and reinvesting the budget into higher-quality food, personalized details, and a better experience for the guests who are there. What is a honeymoon fund registry? A honeymoon fund is a registry option where guests contribute money toward the couple’s honeymoon instead of buying physical gifts. Couples can set up specific experiences (cooking class, excursion, hotel stay) or a general travel fund. It is especially popular among couples who already live together and do not need traditional household items.

title: How we *had* to build OceanOracle
summary: How we were forced to become the first company to build a visual AI for documents
body_text: How we *had* to build OceanOracle How we were forced to become the first company to build a visual AI for documents Hrishi Olickel Published on 1st Feb 2024 5 minutes read "We have some PDFs we'd like to ask questions to. Is that something you can add to your AI?" This was the question that started us down a path that involved a lot of toil and trouble, and how we ended up with a genuine improvement over state-of-the-art RAG solutions. RAG stands for Retrieval-Augmented-Generation, which is the current umbrella term that covers methods for giving AI access to information that they don't already know - like your pdf. Modern AI is a lot like a fresh college graduate - they know a little about everything, but not much about any specific thing - and definitely not your documents. Modern RAG solutions function the same way as equipping this new grad with a good librarian. When a question is asked, this librarian can retrieve the right pages from the right books, the new grad (the AI) can then read them and try to answer your question. Here's the story. Looking for a solution When we were asked to integrate pdfs and unstructured information into our AI, our immediate response was to think that someone would have already done it. Very large companies exist in the space of chat with pdf , and the sector is projected to grow even further. It seemed reasonable to us that off-the-shelf solutions had to exist that could assimilate reasonably sized pdfs and answer questions based on them. Recommended Reading Generative AI: Act Two Unfortunately, none of the solutions we tried really worked. The biggest problem was question complexity. This is easy to illustrate. Let's take this article as an example. At the simplest level, we can ask: 'What is question complexity?' Most RAG systems out there can answer this question with reasonable success. The question has words that are present in the text, and right after this article mentions 'question complexity', I go on to explain the answer. Let's go one level higher: 'Did Greywing find an off-the-shelf solution to their problem?' This is harder because the answer requires the libraries to fetch sections of this article that talk about us trying to find off-the-shelf solutions, and nothing else. Other sections - where we talk about the solution we built - will be confusing, and likely lead to an answer of 'Yes'. One more level: None of the products we tried in the retrieval space were able to answer questions where a direct answer was not already in the document. This was already a problem - but then we got handed another one. They sent over some test documents. More troubles The documents they sent over were hundreds of pages that looked like this: Complex schematics, pipe diagrams, UI frames, with high density of information per page. Knowing the visual relationship between elements is the only way to tell someone how to traverse one part of the ship and another, or how to operate a particular screen. At this point we were entirely in no-man's-land: there really aren't any products that would work with this data. Even the ones that claim an ability to use visual data usually go through an OCR step where the images are converted to text, which is then operated on. We needed to build our own. VisionRAG takes form The key core component in our solution made use of a new development in the world of AI that was only a few weeks old at the time: Multi-modal LLMs . Beginning to be called Vision Models today, these are Transformer models (exactly like ChatGPT), that have been given the gift of sight. By encoding images in place of text (through systems far too complex to explain here), these models can really see information - they can understand spatial relationships, they can identify objects and items, and they can read text in relation to the information on a page. Using these models however is far from easy. How they can be steered and made useful is still an open field of study, and it took us three weeks and all of our expertise to understand how they can be used to understand a document (or multiple), and how to use them. Once we did, we had an initial prototype that could process large visual documents, and answer questions. However, we still hadn't solved the problem of question complexity. How do we answer questions that would actually be useful to humans? VisionRAG becomes WalkingRAG The key to us seemed to be the relationships contained in the documents themselves - and in considering how we approach these problems as humans. Asking a retrieval system to find the right pages and give you a perfect answer in a single shot seems too much - even the best humans couldn't always flip to the right pages to answer complicated questions. So what do we do? We read the pages we can find, and use them to understand which pages we should look at next. If you read closely, the information you find will tell you where to look next - or where you shouldn't. In a nutshell, that's how WalkingRAG - which powers Ocean Oracle - works. When we import documents, we extract relationships - references, topics, section names, etc - from the pages in the pdf. These tell us where to look for more information when we look at a page. Our AI retrieves the right information using a completely new retrieval system developed in-house, then uses those pages to understand where to look next. Even better, it does those things in parallel - to save time and cost. Recommended Watch Greywing announces Ocean Oracle Far better than a librarian and a college grad, WalkingRAG functions more like a team of librarians at your command, working together and looking through multiple documents - taking notes and collecting parts of the answer until they've got all of it. The future This is what we have today. WalkingRAG is turning out to be a completely novel system that promises AI that can truly understand and traverse the information we've created as humans - to serve as a copilot and a subject matter expert for our organizations and engineers. I use it every day to understand large documents, and it's something we're excited to be delivering to anyone that will find it helpful. title: Herbalife Named to TIME's List of America’s Best Companies 2026
summary: Herbalife has been named to TIME's America's Best Companies 2026 list, recognizing excellence in employee satisfaction, financial performance and ESG.
body_text: Recognition highlights strong performance in employee satisfaction, financial strength, and ESG transparency Herbalife, a premier health and wellness company, community and platform, has been named to TIME’s list of America’s Best Companies 2026 . This prestigious award is presented in collaboration with Statista, the world-leading statistics portal and industry ranking provider. The list recognizes organizations that demonstrate excellence across three core areas: employee satisfaction, sustained financial performance, and environmental, social and governance (ESG) transparency. “Being named to TIME’s list of America’s Best Companies reflects the strength of our employees, our independent distributors, and the culture we’ve built across Herbalife,” said Herbalife Chief Executive Officer, Stephan Gratziani. “This recognition highlights our continued focus on delivering strong performance, supporting our people, and operating responsibly across our business.” The list evaluated U.S. companies with more than $100 million in revenue in the most recent fiscal year, with 1,000 companies ultimately included on the list. Rankings are based on input from approximately 217,000 employee surveys assessing workplace culture, compensation, and employer reputation. Financial performance is evaluated using multi-year revenue, profitability, and asset growth metrics, while ESG evaluation considers environmental impact, social responsibility, and governance practices. For over 45 years, Herbalife has empowered millions of people to reach their nutrition, health and wellness goals through science-backed products and the individual coaching provided by its network of independent distributors. With approximately 8,500 employees globally and more than 2 million independent distributors across over 90 markets, Herbalife operates a global nutrition and wellness platform serving millions of customers worldwide. The dedication and collaboration of its employees and distributors have propelled Herbalife to become the #1 active and lifestyle nutrition brand in the world [1] and the #1 protein shake in the world [2] . For more information about Herbalife, visit www.herbalife.com . (1) Source: Euromonitor; CH2026ed, active & lifestyle nutrition as weight management & wellbeing, sports nutrition and vitamins & dietary supplements definitions; combined % RSP share GBO for 2025. (2) Source: Euromonitor; CH2026ed, protein shake as sports protein powder, sports protein RTDs, meal replacement, supplement nutrition drinks & protein supplements; combined % RSP share GBO for 2025. RSP = Retail Selling Price; GBO = Global Brand Owner; RTD = Ready to Drink About Herbalife. Herbalife is a premier health and wellness company, community and platform that has been changing people's lives with great nutrition products and a business opportunity for its independent distributors since 1980. The Company offers science-backed products to consumers in more than 90 markets through entrepreneurial distributors who provide one-on-one coaching and a supportive community that inspires their customers to embrace a healthier, more active lifestyle to live their best life. For more information, visit https://ir.herbalife.com . Media Contact media@herbalife.com

title: What your customer satisfaction score is really telling you (and what it isn’t)
summary: Learn what your customer satisfaction score measures, where it falls short and which metrics complete the picture.
body_text: Your customer feedback survey results just came back, and the customer satisfaction score looks great. So why does it feel like something’s still off? It’s a fair question. A high customer satisfaction score (CSAT) should mean things are going well, but plenty of businesses see strong scores on paper while customers quietly leave. This isn’t necessarily a sign your survey is broken. It’s just that the score reflects a much narrower question than most people assume. In this article, we’ll break down what a CSAT score actually measures, the ways it can be a limited metric and what to track alongside it to get a fuller, more accurate read on customer experience. What your customer satisfaction score actually captures At its core, a customer satisfaction score is a snapshot. It tells you how someone felt about one specific interaction at that specific moment. It’s not a verdict on the entire relationship, but a judgment based on a single support call, checkout experience or other interaction. When someone rates an interaction, the score is typically based on: Whether their expectations were met in that moment Whether a support interaction worked the way it should have Whether they ran into friction during the interaction Whether your frontline team delivered well Whether their immediate issue actually got resolved That information is essential for determining whether a single touchpoint is designed well and doing its job. What it doesn’t tell you, though, is how that customer feels about your business overall, whether they’ll stick around in the long-term or whether smaller frustrations are quietly piling up somewhere else. Why your CSAT score can’t tell you everything Research from McKinsey suggests that companies that excel at customer journeys have a more distinct competitive advantage than those that simply excel at individual touchpoints. In other words, customers judge their experience as a whole, not as a series of disconnected moments. That’s why CSAT’s insights are so limited. While the score might measure individual moments, it doesn’t reflect how those moments connect or whether friction has been building across the entire experience. After all, a customer can have positive feedback for a helpful support agent, even if they spent the last 30 minutes searching your help center, getting nowhere with a chatbot or trying to fix the problem themselves. The interaction itself might have been excellent, but everything leading up to it wasn’t. CSAT also struggles because customer satisfaction is inherently subjective . The exact same interaction can receive wildly different scores depending on the customer’s expectations, mood, personality or past experiences. One person may be happy with a 5-minute response time so long as their problem’s resolved, while another may write off the experience as bad customer service solely because of the wait time. That variability makes it difficult to know whether a score reflects a genuine problem with the experience or simply a difference in perception. And then there’s the fact that satisfaction doesn’t necessarily translate into actual loyalty. Customer satisfaction is generally accepted to be a precursor to attitudinal loyalty, which is the emotional preference for a brand rather than actual loyal behavior. But research shows that neither satisfaction nor attitudinal loyalty can reliably predict customer repurchase behavior . This is why a customer might report high satisfaction and declare loyalty for a coffee brand, but still grab whatever’s on sale that week. There are simply too many other factors influencing repurchase behavior for one customer satisfaction survey score to account for. A high CSAT score, then, shouldn’t be treated as proof that everything is working perfectly. It’s simply evidence that a particular interaction met expectations. To understand whether customers are genuinely happy and whether they’ll stay, you need a broader view of the experience beyond individual moments. What to measure alongside CSAT If CSAT tells you about a single moment, the next question is: what tells you about everything else? That’s where a few other metrics come in, not to replace CSAT, but to fill in what it can’t see. Metric What it measures What it tells you Where it falls short Customer Satisfaction Score (CSAT) Satisfaction with one interaction Whether that specific touchpoint met expectations Says little about long-term loyalty or behavior Customer Effort Score (CES) Ease of completing an interaction or task How much friction customers experience Doesn’t capture emotional attachment to the brand Net Promoter Score (NPS) Willingness to recommend the business Overall sentiment and advocacy Doesn’t predict whether they’ll actually keep buying Churn Customers who left What customers actually did Doesn’t explain why they left Retention Customers who stayed over time Long-term behavioral loyalty Doesn’t capture how customers feel along the way None of these metrics should replace the others since each one answers a slightly different question. If your goal is to improve customer loyalty rather than just chase a higher survey score, look at all of them to get the fullest picture of customer attitudes and behavior. How to get more out of your CSAT score So where does this leave CSAT? It’s still a valuable metric, but it works best when you use it as part of a broader view of the customer experience. A few adjustments can make it more useful: Break CSAT scores down by interaction type instead of blending them into one number. A single average CSAT score can hide a lot. Support calls, billing questions and onboarding touchpoints all carry different expectations, so tracking them separately makes it easier to spot exactly where friction is building and which specific touchpoints need attention. Pair CSAT with other interaction-level metrics like CES and FCR. Satisfaction doesn’t always tell the full story of what happened during an interaction. A customer might rate a conversation highly because a rep was friendly and helpful, even if the process itself was frustrating or required multiple follow-ups. Looking at CSAT alongside metrics like Customer Effort Score (CES) and First Call Resolution (FCR) shows whether customers not only felt good about the interaction, but also whether they were able to get their issue resolved quickly and easily. Watch for flat or high CSAT alongside rising churn. This combination is one of the clearest early warning signs that satisfaction and loyalty have quietly split. When it shows up, it’s usually a cue to look at how well the broader customer journey is delivering. You also want to consider elements outside of the interaction itself, like pricing, competition and unmet needs. Ultimately, CSAT is most valuable when it’s used as an investigative tool, rather than a number to chase. The score itself matters less than the insights it can lead you to. Turn customer feedback into better customer experiences CSAT is still an important metric. It just works best when you look beyond the number itself. The businesses that get the most from customer feedback are the ones that combine customer satisfaction scores with other signals to understand what’s really happening across the customer journey. That also means looking at the conversations driving the scores. This is where tools like Ooma’s AI suite can help. Alongside helping customers get answers faster through features like an AI receptionist and AI answering machine, it can also surface patterns across conversations with call topic organization, sentiment analysis and other insights. These details can give teams a clearer picture of what customers are experiencing and where there’s room to improve.

title: WA - Daniel Schroeder
summary: Daniel Schroeder is senior vice president for Western Alliance Bank’s Private Client Group. Based in San Diego, he provides high-touch private banking and customized credit solutions to business owners, executives and investors.
body_text: Daniel Schroeder Senior Vice President Private Client Group p (619) 233-2246 [email protected] Daniel Schroeder is senior vice president for Western Alliance Bank’s Private Client Group. Based in San Diego, he provides high-touch private banking and customized credit solutions to business owners, executives and investors and has particular expertise in the needs of family offices. Mr. Schroeder integrates the bank’s Private Client Group services with each client’s broader advisory team, including wealth managers, attorneys and CPAs, to ensure every banking decision supports their long-term wealth strategy. Mr. Schroeder joined Western Alliance in 2026 with more than 20 years of experience serving high-net-worth clients. He brings particular expertise in credit strategy, relationship management, and banking and treasury management, as well as the biotech, private equity and real estate sectors. Before joining Western Alliance, he was director of Banking and Lending Services at Sapient Capital, where he led strategy for client banking relationships and advised clients on credit solutions. He previously served as executive director at JPMorgan Chase and spent eight years managing private banking and lending services for clients at First Republic Bank. Earlier in his career, he held a dual role as director of Banking and Lending and director of Corporate Trust Services for a large family office. A graduate of San Diego State University, he also completed the Executive Leadership Development Program (Levels I and II) at the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania. About Us Western Alliance Bank Western Alliance Bancorporation (NYSE: WAL) is one of the country’s top-performing banking companies and has ranked as a top U.S. bank by American Banker and Bank Director since 2016. Its primary subsidiary, Western Alliance Bank, is a leading national bank for business that puts customers first, delivering tailored business banking solutions and consumer products backed by outstanding, personalized service and specific expertise in more than 30 industries and sectors. With $90 billion in assets and offices nationwide, Western Alliance excels at helping businesses of all sizes capitalize on their opportunities to solve today and succeed tomorrow.

title: How Mentorship Helped Me Land My First IT Job: Real Success Stories from NGT Academy Career Changers
summary: How Mentorship Helped Me Land My First IT Job | Real NGT Stories
body_text: Breaking into IT or cybersecurity can feel overwhelming, especially for adults changing careers, veterans, or anyone without a traditional tech degree. At NGT Academy, we believe that mentorship bridges this gap, transforming motivated learners into job-ready professionals. This article explores exactly how mentorship helped me land my first IT job —with real stories and step-by-step insight for anyone considering the leap into tech. If you are looking to switch careers into IT, move up from an entry-level role, or want hands-on training that leads straight to employment, this guide is for you. You will see how mentorship, skills-based learning, and community support can make all the difference. How does mentorship actually help you land your first IT job? Mentorship connects you with experienced professionals who provide personalized guidance, practical feedback, and structured accountability, turning theory into real-world skills and helping you confidently navigate job searches, interviews, and career transitions into IT or cybersecurity. The Power of Mentorship in Tech Career Change For many career changers, self-study or online tutorials are not enough. The tech world moves fast, and practical skills matter more than ever. Mentorship accelerates growth by offering: Personalized learning plans that target your goals and fill knowledge gaps Real-world problem solving through labs, projects, and simulated scenarios Emotional support to overcome impostor syndrome and keep moving forward Professional networking and insider advice for interviews and job applications At NGT Academy, mentorship is woven into every program, supporting students from the first lesson through job placement. Real Success Story: From Help Desk to Cybersecurity Engineer Consider Alex, a 32-year-old with five years of help desk experience but no computer science degree. Like many, Alex wanted higher pay, job security, and a more meaningful role. Mentorship at NGT Academy provided the roadmap, accountability, and industry insight that made his transition possible. Alex’s Step-by-Step Journey with Mentorship Building a Solid Foundation: Alex reviewed networking, operating systems, and security basics with mentor-led labs and feedback. Specialization and Skill Development: Guided by mentors, Alex specialized in SOC analysis, mastering threat monitoring and incident response via hands-on simulations and CTF competitions. Certifications and Portfolio Building: With a mentor’s encouragement, Alex earned his CompTIA Security+ and built a public portfolio, including vulnerability assessments and malware analysis write-ups. Career Coaching and Job Search: Mentors helped polish Alex’s resume, practice interviews, and expand his professional network. The result? Alex landed a cybersecurity engineer role in under a year with a 35% salary increase. Mentorship was the constant thread guiding each step. Why Hands-On Learning and Mentorship Matter Tech employers want candidates who can prove their skills. NGT Academy’s blend of mentorship and hands-on labs ensures students are not just learning theory, but practicing job-ready tasks. Whether configuring firewalls, analyzing phishing simulations, or documenting projects on GitHub, guided mentorship transforms learning into real-world competence. Transferable Skills for Career Changers Troubleshooting and Incident Response: Help desk experience translates directly into problem-solving in security roles. Networking Fundamentals: Understanding TCP/IP, VPNs, and firewalls forms the backbone of IT and cybersecurity roles. User Support: Communication skills are crucial for translating technical solutions to non-technical stakeholders. Basic Scripting and Automation: Skills in PowerShell or Bash help automate repetitive tasks and streamline workflows. Mentors help students recognize and leverage these abilities, boosting confidence and employability. What Are the Common Challenges for Career Changers? Switching careers into IT or cybersecurity involves hurdles. Time management, technical doubt, and a lack of experience are all common. Here’s how mentorship addresses these challenges: Time Management: Mentors help structure weekly study blocks and keep you accountable, making progress possible even with a busy schedule. Overcoming Impostor Syndrome: Community support and visible progress, guided by mentors, help defeat self-doubt. Gaining Real Experience: Mentors connect students to volunteer security projects, CTF events, and networking opportunities to build portfolios and confidence. For more advice on hands-on learning, check our post: Help desk experience . Key Steps to Land Your First IT or Cybersecurity Job with Mentorship Set Clear Goals: Define your desired role (e.g., SOC analyst, network engineer) and identify the skills required. Engage in Structured Training: Choose programs with hands-on labs and real-world projects. Work with a Mentor: Meet regularly with mentors for feedback, accountability, and industry insights. Build a Portfolio: Document labs, simulations, and independent projects on LinkedIn or GitHub. Earn Certifications: Obtain credentials like CompTIA Security+ and CySA+ to validate your skills. Prepare for the Job Search: Use career coaching for resume reviews, interview preparation, and networking strategies. Career Outcomes and Long-Term Growth Mentorship does not end when you land your first IT job. Many NGT Academy graduates, like Alex, go on to mentor others and advance to senior roles. The tech industry rewards continuous learning, specialization, and leadership—qualities fostered through ongoing mentorship. The demand for IT and cybersecurity professionals remains high, with salaries and opportunities growing each year. Your journey can lead to specialized roles in penetration testing, compliance, or network defense, and even six-figure salaries with experience. Ready to Transform Your Career? If you are ready for a new career in IT or cybersecurity and want the support of expert mentors, explore our program for a proven path to job readiness. Mentorship, hands-on labs, and career coaching are included every step of the way. Curious about how NGT Academy helps people from all backgrounds achieve tech careers? Learn more about our mission and community impact here. FAQ How does mentorship at NGT Academy work for career changers? Mentorship at NGT Academy pairs students with experienced IT professionals who guide them through hands-on training, provide feedback, and support job search preparation. What are the main benefits of mentorship for landing a first IT job? Mentorship offers personalized feedback, real-world project guidance, interview preparation, and accountability, which accelerates skill development and job readiness. Can I succeed in IT or cybersecurity without a traditional degree? Yes, many NGT Academy graduates have launched successful careers without a degree by focusing on hands-on skills, certifications, and building a strong project portfolio. What roles can I pursue after completing NGT Academy programs? Graduates commonly land roles like SOC Analyst, Network Engineer, Vulnerability Assessment Analyst, and Incident Response Analyst. How long does it usually take to land a first IT job with mentorship?
